pending_commit.commit_message: UPSTREAM: drm/i915: Handle failure from 2nd stage HDCP auth We enable the HDCP encryption as a part of first stage authentication. So when second stage authentication fails, we need to disable the HDCP encryption and signalling. This patch ensures that, when hdcp authentication fails, HDCP encryption and signalling is turned off. v2: Dropped connector ref passing to auth [Seanpaul] Moved the call to disable_hdcp() to enable_hdcp() [Seanpaul] v3: No Changes. Added the Reveiwed-by tag. Signed-off-by: Ramalingam C <ramalingam.c@intel.com> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org> Signed-off-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org> Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/1517609350-10698-2-git-send-email-ramalingam.c@intel.com (cherry picked from commit a01244967d4311afb1a8e068184c2a30202025f5) Signed-off-by: Ramalingam C <ramalingam.c@intel.com> Change-Id: I995cb63f5f122e7a1d6233b65918e21793b4e9e2 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/908508 Commit-Ready: Sean Paul <seanpaul@google.com> Tested-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@google.com> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@google.com>

UPSTREAM: drm/i915: Stop encryption for repeater with no sink If a HDCP repeater is detected with zero downstream devices, HDCP spec approves either of below actions: 1. Dont continue on second stage authentication. Disable encryption. 2. Continue with second stage authentication excluding the KSV list and on success, continue encryption. Since disable encryption is agreed, repeater is not expected to have its own display. So there is no consumption of the display content in such setup. Hence, incase of repeater with zero device count, this patch fails the HDCP authentication and stops the HDCP encryption. v2: Rephrased commit msg and added comments in code [Seanpaul] v3: No changes. Added Reviewed-by tag. Signed-off-by: Ramalingam C <ramalingam.c@intel.com> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org> Signed-off-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org> Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/1517609350-10698-3-git-send-email-ramalingam.c@intel.com (cherry picked from commit f179a2fc2e23ff623344717eec3b8a443a57222a) Signed-off-by: Ramalingam C <ramalingam.c@intel.com> Change-Id: Ic79573a1da172c7a6739729297f88b86ac594b04 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/908509 Commit-Ready: Sean Paul <seanpaul@google.com> Tested-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@google.com> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@google.com>

UPSTREAM: drm/i915: Detect panel's hdcp capability DP HDCP1.4 spec mandates that An can be written to panel only after detecting the panel's hdcp capability. For DP 0th Bit of Bcaps register indicates the panel's hdcp capability For HDMI valid BKSV indicates the panel's hdcp capability. For HDMI it is optional to detect the panel's hdcp capability before An Write. v2: Added comments explaining the need for action [Seanpaul]. Made panel's hdcp capability detection optional for hdmi [Seanpaul]. Defined a func for reading bcaps for DP [Seanpaul]. v3: Removed the NULL initialization [Seanpaul]. BACKPORT: thermal: Enhance thermal_zone_device_update for events Added one additional parameter to thermal_zone_device_update() to provide caller with an optional capability to specify reason. Currently this event is used by user space governor to trigger different processing based on event code. Also it saves an additional call to read temperature when the event is received. FROMGIT: amdgpu/dc: Fix enum mismatch in calls to program_color_matrix() The driver passes GRAPHICS_CSC_ADJUST_TYPE_SW of type enum graphics_csc_adjust_type to program_color_matrix(), however the function expects a parameter of type enum grph_color_adjust_option. Supposedly the intention was to pass GRPH_COLOR_MATRIX_SW, which has the same value as GRAPHICS_CSC_ADJUST_TYPE_SW, so the mismatch didn't cause any trouble. arc-networkd: Read the interface table id from sysfs This change stops reading /data/misc/net/rt_tables from the Android filesystem since there were some recent changes in the Android side that cause the arc0 interface to be removed from that file occasionally, causing arc-networkd to crash pretty often. Instead, this uses the same algorithm that Android uses to derive the table ids from the interface name: get the interface index (a-la ioctl(fd, SIOCGIFINDEX, ...)) and add a constant to it. In order to avoid entering a net namespace just to perform this operation, this change reads the index from /sys/class/net/arc0/ifindex (within the container's point of view).
